Introducing psa > Structured Diagnostics

Structured Diagnostics

Status: landed. psa’s errors are structured: every diagnostic carries a stable code, a named rule, one plain-language message, the position (or positions) it blames, and — where the rule has one — an actionable fix hint. The same diagnostic renders as text for humans and as JSON for tools. Runtime panics use a parallel numeric code table, and one command, psa explain, explains either kind of code. The system was built by the 2026-11-26 errors line and integrated into the master tree; its close-out batch landed in 2026-11-28 (sapy d696d65a), completing the panic table and putting the comparison test suite in the repository.

Every compile-time error has a stable code

Codes are grouped by the stage that refuses the program: PSA-L### for the lexer, PSA-P### for the parser, PSA-E#### for the emitter (type and ownership checks), and PSA-H### for failures of the host pipeline itself (for example PSA-H002, input file not found). The registry holds 345 unique codes. A diagnostic the registry cannot classify falls back to a visibly generic code (PSA-L900 / PSA-P900 / PSA-E9000) rather than borrowing a specific one — and the in-repository audit of all 13 reject examples finds none of them on a fallback code.

A diagnostic may carry more than one position: each site has a file, line, column and a role. A use-after-move error, for instance, points at the use as the primary site and at the move as a second site, because both halves are needed to fix it.

A worked example (measured, verbatim)

This three-line program moves a list and then uses the dead binding:

xs = [1, 2, 3]
ys = xs
print(xs)

psa check moved.psa refuses it (exit code 1) with:

error[PSA-E1001]: use of `xs` after it was moved
  --> moved.psa:3:7
   | print(xs)
   |       ^
   = site: move (line 2:6)
   | ys = xs
   |      ^
note: container assignment moves the value; the binding is dead until it is re-bound
hint: re-bind `xs` before line 3, or bind a copy at line 2

The text form gives the code, both sites with source excerpts and carets, a note explaining the rule, and a hint that says what to change.

Machine-readable output: --error-format=json

The global flag --error-format=text|json is accepted before or after the subcommand (the environment variable PSA_ERROR_FORMAT is the fallback). The same check in JSON form prints one object:

{"code":"PSA-E1001","rule":"use-after-move","kind":"emit","file":"moved.psa","sites":[{"line":3,"col":7,"role":"use","snippet":"print(xs)"},{"line":2,"col":6,"role":"move","snippet":"ys = xs"}],"message":"use of `xs` after it was moved","note":"container assignment moves the value; the binding is dead until it is re-bound","hint":"re-bind `xs` before line 3, or bind a copy at line 2"}

The fields are the contract: code, rule, kind, file, sites (each with line, column, role and source snippet), message, and the optional note and hint. A diagnostic with no source position (a host failure such as a missing input file) renders an empty sites list rather than inventing one.

Runtime panic codes, and psa explain

Runtime failures panic with a bare numeric code (the source map page explains how the code is traced back to source positions). The codes are not folklore: a machine-readable master table, PANIC-CODES.json in psa_std, is generated from the compiler’s own table and holds 113 keys — 102 codes the compiler actually emits, plus 11 reserved. Each entry records the code, its rule name, a category, a one-line summary, and a fix note where one applies. A checked invariant of the build is that every emitted code is in the table; the one historical violation (77083, emitted but unregistered) was found by that check and repaired by registering it.

psa explain looks a code up, in either family:

$ psa explain 77083
panic 77083 - the module environment was read before it was published (closure runtime invariant; unreachable in a correctly emitted program) (PSA-R77083)
  category: runtime-core
  fix: this is a psa internal invariant, not a problem in your code; please report it with the source file

$ psa explain PSA-E1001
PSA-E1001 (use-after-move)
  use of a name after it was moved; the diagnostic carries two sites (the use and the move)

With --error-format=json, explain answers in the same JSON shape (a runtime code reports as PSA-R77083-style, kind runtime, empty sites). An unknown code fails loudly — psa explain 99999 exits 1 with psa explain: unknown panic code 99999 — rather than guessing.

How this is verified

The landed evidence, re-run on the landing head: the in-repository comparison suite tests-diag passes 34/34 (nine numbered negative cases read in both text and JSON form, the host-level H002 case, and six explain cases including the loud failure on an unknown code); the panic-table check passes (emitted 102 ⊆ table 113); the registry audit over the repository’s 13 reject examples finds 8 with psa codes and 0 on fallback codes; and the positive corpus still emits cleanly, 61/61 with no regression.

Registered gaps (not hidden)

  • Five of the 13 reject examples are still refused downstream, without a psa-level diagnostic. The clearest is lambda capture: psa accepts the program at emit time and the generated code is refused by the host pipeline, reported as an unmapped host diagnostic — the registered code PSA-E5002 exists but is unreachable for that shape. The follow-up batch adds emit-time checks for these shapes; until it lands, those five refusals carry no PSA code and no user-source site.
  • Hints are not yet universal. Of the registry’s 368 message templates, about 269 still have no hint and about 307 no cleaned-up message rewrite. Every one of them has a stable code and rule today; the plain-language pass proceeds in census frequency order.
  • Code 77084 is unassigned. Nothing emits it and it is not in the table; whether to reserve it explicitly is an open decision, recorded rather than silently settled.

Key Points of This Page

  • Every psa error has a stable code (PSA-L/P/E/H families, 345 registered), a rule, positions with roles, a plain message, and a fix hint where the rule has one.
  • --error-format=json renders the same diagnostic as one JSON object with a fixed field contract; position-less diagnostics render empty sites, never invented ones.
  • Runtime panics use a numeric master table (113 keys: 102 emitted, 11 reserved) shipped as PANIC-CODES.json; psa explain explains both families and fails loudly on unknown codes.
  • Verified on the landing head: comparison suite 34/34, panic-table check passes, positive corpus 61/61 unchanged.
  • Registered gaps: five reject shapes still refused downstream without a psa code (PSA-E5002 batch pending), hints not yet universal, code 77084 unassigned.
